title: How mouthpiece opening affects blowing
summary: Too closed a facing flops, too open wastes wind; they discuss trying an H2S.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Do you like it not too wide open then, you think? Or no? Does it make any difference in getting the big tone that you do to have it either wider or more narrow? What do you think?
Yes, it do. See, too close, when it's closed too much, when you blow hard, it'll close and nothing come out. It'll flop. That's right, yeah.
And if it's too wide, you have to blow so hard that you hardly have any wind left. Or too hard, yeah, you hardly have any wind left.
So you have to blow on them, you have to play, it'll take a while for you to find out exactly what you should have. That's right, yeah.

That's right, yeah. Now this one I'm using is the same as Mineta's mouthpiece, it's a Kahn. It's a Kahn? A Kahn mouthpiece. And I find it's a little wider than the average one, you know? Uh-huh. But I find that now I've got used to it, the other ones, they flop. Yeah.
Yeah. Got used to blowing hard. Well, you just, you just, I think you should try one of them H2S. I'd like to do that. What make is that? A Selmer.
All the used to have, you could go, you could go right back to you, you know, on Brow Street.
Yeah. I'd like to do that. Would you say the H2S is a little better than the H1S that you've got?
It would be better for me, I think. Yeah. Of course, now that I got used to this one, I guess the problem would be about the same.
